missed_items: FEATURE CONTRACT — 4 of the 47 daily scalars are never checked for existence, and a missing one silently becomes a constant 0.0 feature. _prepare_sources validates only ACTIVITY_SAFE_SCALARS/SLEEP_SAFE_SCALARS (data.py:659-666), which do NOT contain activity_non_wear, activity_inactivity_alerts, sleep_midpoint_at_delta or sleep_restless. paperlib reads all 47 with `feats[col] = D._numeric(record.get(col))` (paperlib.py:141); a missing column yields None → `float(None)` raises → np.nan (data.py:326-331), so the whole column is NaN, and `_impute_fit` turns an all-NaN column into 0.0 (`np.where(np.isfinite(med), med, 0.0)`, paperlib.py:204). No NaN count is written to any output, so a renamed source column would be undetectable. The reader reported the NaN→median path but not that four feature names are unvalidated.

ACQUISITION-FEATURE CONFLICT — the reader called ACTIVITY_SCALARS 'exactly the paper's 24' without noting that it re-introduces columns the sibling module's own contract forbids. data.py:43-44 states 'Acquisition-related columns such as activity_non_wear, sleep_period_id, and sleep_is_longest are absent', and `_validate_feature_contract` (data.py:626-643) raises on any name containing 'non_wear' or 'count'. paperlib's 69 features include activity_non_wear (paperlib.py:49) and eight `*_count_*` columns (paperlib.py:148, 151), i.e. this feature set would fail that contract — which is never invoked on this path. Paper-faithful (PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:83 lists activity_non_wear) but it means the model may use a wear-time/compliance signal.

DAY-LEVEL CLASS COUNTS ARE NEVER REPORTED — the paper's record-level balance is CN 7,737 / impaired 4,446 (PAPER_PROTOCOL.md:36), the single number by which the day-level diagnostic could be compared to the paper. The EDA writes only subject-level counts (`"class_counts": {"CN": int((y == 0).sum()), "MCI_DEM": int((y == 1).sum())}`, paperlib.py:297 → eda_summary.json:6-9 85/56). The 9,673 diagnostic days have no recorded class split anywhere.

NO GUARD THAT ALL 33 VALIDATION SUBJECTS SURVIVE ALIGNMENT — `_validate` derives its subject list from the aligned Validation frame (paperlib.py:337-338) and then indexes the labels by that list (`y_val.loc[[str(s) for s in v_subjects]]`, paperlib.py:349), so any Validation subject with zero aligned activity/sleep days is silently absent from the hold-out; the count is only reported after the fact (FINAL_REPORT.json:20). The expected 33 / 26-7 contract exists (data.py:119-120) but is never invoked here.

HOLD-OUT ACCURACY IS BELOW ITS OWN MAJORITY BASELINE — the reader printed both numbers but never stated the comparison, which is the relevant reading against the paper's 0.8262 accuracy: `accuracy_threshold_0.5` = 0.6364 vs `all_cn_accuracy` = 0.7879 (FINAL_REPORT.json:22-23), i.e. the 0.5-threshold classifier is worse than predicting CN for everyone. Code: paperlib.py:353-356 `pred = (prob >= 0.5).astype(int)` / `"all_cn_accuracy": float(np.mean(y_val == 0))`.

THE STALE ~0.71 CLAIM IS IN THE MODULE, NOT ONLY THE README — the reader cited README_KO.md:20 and :44, but paperlib.py's own docstring makes the same unreconciled claim: paperlib.py:20-22 'Honest expectation: leakage-free subject-level ROC-AUC is ~0.71 (the ceiling found across every prior experiment)'. Fixing the README alone would leave the source asserting a figure the only recorded run contradicts by 0.19 AUC.

FEATURE IDENTITY IS NEVER PERSISTED — `feat_names` is computed (paperlib.py:292) and used for hold-out column alignment (paperlib.py:339-343) but never written to any output; eda_summary.json records only `"n_features_subject_level": 138` (line 10). The exact 138-column set of the recorded run cannot be reconstructed from the artifacts, which matters precisely because the set deviates from the paper's 72.

DIAGNOSTIC FOLD COUNT IS INHERITED FROM RUN MODE — `leakage_diagnostic(train_daily, folds=config.folds, seed=config.seed)` (paperlib.py:310) takes the same folds as the primary CV, so a smoke run (run.py:121 `dict(repeats=1, folds=3)`) silently turns the paper-style day-level arm into a 3-fold split; nothing in FINAL_REPORT.json records the diagnostic's fold count, only `run_mode`.

SUBJECT-ID HASH IS UNSALTED, VIOLATING THE REFERENCE PRIVACY CONTRACT — the reader listed this as a neutral difference rather than a defect. `_hash` is `hashlib.sha256(str(s).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]` (paperlib.py:282-283), applied at paperlib.py:304 when writing oof_predictions_hashed.csv; ASSUMPTIONS.md:13 (A05) requires a *salted* SHA-256 prefix. Since the raw identifiers are e-mail addresses, an unsalted digest is invertible by enumeration, so the committed OOF file is not de-identified to the project's own standard.
